To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the medaka mii mutant exhibits defects in the formation of the left right body axis and the kidney due to the loss of dynein intermediate chain 2.
dynein axonal intermediate chain 2 (Dnai2) proteins are essential for the left-right (L-R) polarity and kidney development through the regulation of ciliary beating.
the mii mutant exhibits left-right body axis defects and polycystin kidney disease, and that these are caused by defects in the cilia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of LR body asymmetry and PKD.
how cilia function to regulate LR polarity and renal function.
the identification and characterization of the genes responsible for the left-right body asymmetry and the kidney formation in medaka.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the loss of Dnai2 function leads to ciliary defects and the development of PCD and PKD.
Dnai proteins control LR polarity, kidney formation and PKD through the regulation of cilia motility.
Dnai proteins control LR polarity, cilia motility and kidney formation through their function in ODA formation in cilia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Dnai proteins regulate the LR body axis and kidney formation in medaka by controlling the formation and/or function of cilia.
the mii mutation causes a defect in the ODA of the cilia in KV, which is a left-sided organ, resulting in a failure to establish left-right asymmetry in the body axis.
the loss of dnais leads to ciliary dysfunctions in both KV and kidney, which results in the loss of nodal flows and PKD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Dnai proteins are required for the formation of the left–right body axis and kidney.
cilia are required to establish LR asymmetry, and that defects in this process can lead to kidney diseases.
Dnai-2 is required for cilia function in both kidney and KV.
